problem: The transform integral is printed as '∫₀∞ f(t)e−stdt'. The exponent is not raised, so a student reads it as e minus s times t times dt instead of e raised to −st.
fix: Write it as L{f(t)} = ∫₀∞ f(t)e<sup>−st</sup>dt, and say 'the exponent −st multiplies the dummy time variable'.

problem: 'A is the amplitude or strength, in the same units as the signal' is true only for the step. For A·t·1(t), A is the slope (signal units per second); for A·(t²/2)·1(t), A is an acceleration-like constant (signal units per second squared); for A·δ(t), A is area (signal units times seconds). A student may write the wrong units in an answer.
fix: Say: 'For A·1(t), A is the step amplitude in signal units. For A·t·1(t), A is the slope in signal units per second. For A·(t²/2)·1(t), A is in signal units per second squared. For A·δ(t), A is the impulse strength, in signal units times seconds.'
